subject: botany
question_text: What is meant by manuals and monographs?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Manual
lines: Manuals give information for the identification
of the names of species found in an area.
steps.why: A manual is the working companion to a flora — it carries the information needed to identify and name the species of one area.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two definitions. A manual covers the species of an AREA; a monograph covers ONE taxon.
Writing 'a manual is a handbook' with no botany content. Say what it identifies: species of an area.
steps.memory_tip: Manual — Many species of one area. Monograph — Mono, one taxon only.
steps.margin_note: One sentence each. Keep the two definitions clearly separate.

steps.label: Monograph

lines.text: Monograph: information on any one taxon

lines: It gives a complete account of a single
taxon — one family, one genus or one species.
steps.why: 'Mono' means one — a monograph collects the information on a single taxon, at any rank.
common_mistakes: Writing that a monograph covers all the plants of an area. That is a flora or a manual, not a monograph.
steps.memory_tip: Mono = one. A monograph is the one-taxon book.
steps.margin_note: The boxed line alone earns the mark; the rank examples are supporting detail.

insider_note: The pair is marked as a contrast — 'species of an area' on the manual line and 'any one taxon' on the monograph line.
